sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers central Riverton between 4th Street and Broad Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy Division) along the right edge. Fulton, Cinnaminson and Howard run across the sheet between 4th and 5th Streets and on to Broad; Main crosses the lower part diagonally towards the railroad, and Church Lane runs parallel to it along the bottom. The upper blocks are residential, with large frame dwellings on Fulton and Cinnaminson. The Riverton Public School (brick, heated by hot air, with a stage) stands in the block between 4th and 5th Streets south of Cinnaminson. The block between 5th Street and Broad south of Cinnaminson holds the fire department, a laundry, wagon and tool sheds, and at its Broad Street end a cement-floored garage for 35 cars with concrete-block additions. North of Cinnaminson near Broad is a second garage for 20 cars. Main Street is the business street: a row of stores and dwellings on its south side between 5th and Broad includes a bakery and an auto repair shop on Church Lane, and a three-sided brick building at Howard and Main houses a lodge room and hall over feed stores. At the right, beside the tracks, is the railroad passenger depot. The top margin is marked as Sheet 13 and the left as Sheet 13, the lower right as Sheet 3 and the bottom as Sheet 6. A short length of Cinnaminson Street is lettered east of the railroad at the top right. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: Riverton Public School; fire department; passenger depot of the Pennsylvania Railroad.
Church Lane is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name; Broad Street junctions were not used for control (roadway and railroad share one right of way).

50 ft. Fulton, Cinnaminson, Howard, Main (diagonal) between 4th and 5th to Broad and the P.R.R.; Riverton Public School, fire department, passenger depot; Church Lane along the bottom. Single part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the central business blocks of Riverton at 50 feet to an inch. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy Division) runs diagonally up the left side of the sheet with Broad Street beside it, and the sheet is turned so that the streets east of the tracks run square to the page. Cedar crosses the top, Cinnaminson and Main cross the middle and Lippincott Avenue the bottom, and 7th Street forms the right edge; Harrison Avenue runs south from Main between the railroad and the blocks. North of Cinnaminson, block 8 holds a row of frame dwellings. Between Cinnaminson and Main, block 9 contains the post office, the Cinnaminson National Bank, a wagon shed, a printing shop and dwellings, while beside the tracks stand Jos. T. Evans's feed, coal and lumber works with an ice house, lumber storage, a coke bin and a footwalk, served by a track on trestle. South of Main, block 10 (254) holds the Collis lumber and feed yard (J. S. Collis & Son: lumber shed, coal bins, hay and feed store, lumber storage), a hardware and paint store, a plumber and tin shop, club rooms and a pool room, with dwellings and double houses along Main and 7th Street. Below Lippincott Avenue are an auto repair shop and further dwellings in blocks 11 and 52. The left margin shows parts of Sheets 2 and 6, and the right margin Sheet 12. A compass rose is drawn in the open ground at upper left. Water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets.
notes: Harrison Avenue is today's Harrison Street; its modern line is skewed and displaced from the drawn street, so it was left out of the control.
Control: four junctions on 7th Street plus six points carried from sheets 10 and 11 along the A-B match line at the bottom (block lines and a concrete-block auto house drawn on both sheets).

50 ft. Broad and the P.R.R. diagonal at left; Cedar, Cinnaminson, Main, Lippincott east of the tracks, Harrison Av., 7th Street at right; post office, Cinnaminson National Bank, Jos. T. Evans and J. S. Collis & Son coal, feed and lumber yards. Single part, drawn square to the page (rotation -26). Harrison Avenue left out (modern line skewed, 11-17 m off); Broad and rail points left out. Control: 7th Street junctions plus points carried from sheets 10 and 11 along the A-B match line.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the river front of Riverton between Penn and Thomas Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Bank Avenue runs along the Delaware River at the left, with the shore and a stone retaining wall drawn beside it; Front runs down the middle and 2nd Street forms the right edge. Penn crosses the top, Lippincott Avenue the middle and Thomas Avenue the bottom, and the sixteen-foot Maple Lane runs east from Front between Lippincott and Thomas. The long block between Bank Avenue and Front north of Lippincott (block 256) is divided into deep river-front lots with large frame dwellings, one of them stone in the first storey, and a stone apartment house near Lippincott; automobile houses and other outbuildings stand at the Front ends of the lots. South of Lippincott, block 204 holds three large stone-faced residences with a laundry, an auto house, a boat house and storage buildings. Between Front and 2nd Street are a garage on Penn, scattered dwellings in block 15, two large houses in the block south of Lippincott, and in block 205 along Maple Lane and 2nd Street a group of small dwellings and double houses. The top margin is marked as Sheet 13, the right as Sheet 5 and the bottom as Sheet 7. Four- and six-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets.
notes: Front on this sheet is today's Carriage House Lane.
Maple Lane (16 ft) was left out of the control: its junction with Front was 7 m off and with 2nd Street 3 m.
Bank Avenue junctions with Penn and Lippincott were not detected; the river side of Bank Avenue is open.
50 ft. River side: Bank Avenue along the Delaware, Penn, Lippincott, Maple Lane, Thomas, Front Street. Single part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the blocks of Riverton between 2nd Street on the left and 4th Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Lippincott Avenue and Thomas Avenue run diagonally up the page to the right. Penn runs along the top, Lippincott Avenue crosses the middle, and Thomas Avenue runs along the bottom; the sixteen-foot Maple Lane lies between them and Church Lane, a narrow way, crosses the upper right between Lippincott Avenue and Penn, parallel to Lippincott. 3rd Street enters from Penn and ends against the blocks near the middle. The upper blocks (numbered 17, 20 and 21) hold a row of small frame dwellings fronting Penn, Mt. Zion A.M.E. Church with its parish dwellings, a chapel and Calvary Presbyterian Church on Church Lane, and large detached houses on big lots, among them a stone-faced residence with a blue-coloured outline. Between Lippincott Avenue and Maple Lane stand several substantial dwellings on deep lots, one with a long frame addition, and between Maple Lane and Thomas Avenue are dwellings with automobile houses, a chicken-coop group and a large dwelling with a coloured cellar. Much of the left side is empty ground belonging to Sheet 4. The corner of the sheet holds a compass rose and the Riverton oval. Margins refer to Sheets 13 above, 4 at the left, 6 at the right and 8 below. Water mains of four and six inches run in the streets.
notes: Maple Lane (16 ft) and Church Lane (not in OpenStreetMap) were left out of the control.

50 ft. Penn, Church Lane, Lippincott, Maple Lane, Thomas between 2nd and 4th; 3rd Street stub from Penn; Mt. Zion A.M.E. and Calvary Presbyterian churches. Single part. Maple Lane and Church Lane left out.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the residential blocks of Riverton between 4th Street on the left and Broad on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally up the page to the right. Main and Fifth Street occupy the top, with Penn Street entering from the left beside 4th Street. Three long diagonal streets cross the sheet: Church Lane at the top, Lippincott Avenue through the middle, and Thomas Avenue along the bottom, with the narrow Maple Lane running between Lippincott Avenue and Thomas Avenue. The blocks are divided into long narrow lots, each with a frame dwelling of two or three storeys and small outbuildings, with larger houses on wider lots, one with a round bay and one with a coloured outline. A larger pink-coloured building with a cross-shaped plan stands on the block between Main and Church Lane, and near Broad at the right a plumber and tin shop is drawn. Lot numbers run in the 900 and 400 series along the street fronts. Six- and eight-inch water mains are drawn in the streets and at Broad, with fire hydrants marked. The lower right of the sheet is blank, and the margins refer to Sheets 13 above left, 5 at the left, 3 and 10 at the right and 9 below. A compass rose and the Riverton oval stand at the top.
notes: Maple Lane and Church Lane were left out of the control (a 16 ft lane and a street not in OpenStreetMap).
Broad is Broad Street (west of the railroad) in OpenStreetMap; the junction with Main lies off the sheet.
50 ft. Main, Fifth St., Penn St., Church Lane, Lippincott, Maple Lane, Thomas between 4th Street and Broad. Single part. Broad Street (west of the tracks) used; Maple Lane, Church Lane left out.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south-west corner of Riverton on the Delaware River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, between Thomas Avenue at the top and Elm Avenue, the borough limits with Palmyra, at the bottom. Bank runs along the river bank at the left with the shore drawn beside it, Front runs down the middle, and 2nd Street forms the right edge; Linden Avenue crosses the sheet halfway down. The two large blocks between Bank and Front (207 and 208) are river-front estates: big detached dwellings, three of them of stone in the first storey and one of brick, with a carriage house of cement, a play house, a tool house, a boat house, a laundry, a metal-frame greenhouse, wagon sheds and other outbuildings set in open grounds. Between Front and 2nd Street the blocks hold a few frame dwellings, coops and a tool house in block 206, and in block 209 a row of four small dwellings along Elm Avenue near 2nd Street. Below Elm Avenue the sheet is left blank with the note See Map of Palmyra, N.J., and the lower right corner is lettered with Elm Av. and Morgan St., the streets continuing into Palmyra. Bank turns inland at the bottom left where a six-inch water pipe crosses the borough line. Sixteen-, eight-, six- and four-inch water pipes are drawn in Elm Avenue, Bank, Linden Avenue and Thomas Avenue.
notes: Front (Front Street) on this sheet is today's Carriage House Lane, which follows its line between Penn Street and Linden Avenue.
Elm Avenue is the borough limits with Palmyra; Morgan Street is today's Morgan Avenue in Palmyra.
Control is six junctions on Thomas and Linden Avenues only; nothing along Elm Avenue was detected.
50 ft. River side: Bank Avenue along the Delaware, Thomas, Linden, Elm to the Palmyra line. Single part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers a block of Riverton between 2nd Street on the left and 4th Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the cross streets run diagonally up the page to the right. Thomas Avenue crosses the upper part, Linden Avenue the middle, and Elm Avenue forms the bottom boundary, where a dash-dot line marks the borough limits and the lettering 'See Map of Palmyra N.J.' covers the ground beyond. Morgan Street appears as a stub in the lower left corner. The large blocks are mostly open lots with scattered frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, and a few outbuildings and coops; one structure near the left is labelled as a boarded-over building. Between Linden Avenue and Elm Avenue (block 210) the lots are narrower, with a row of small dwellings and a print shop beside Elm Avenue, and a pink-coloured dwelling and a tile-roofed building are drawn among the yellow frame houses. Lot numbers in the 200, 1200, 1400 and 1500 series run along the street fronts. Four-inch water pipes are drawn in 2nd Street, Thomas Avenue, Linden Avenue and 4th Street, with fire hydrants at several corners. The margins refer to Sheet 5 above, 7 at the left and 9 at the right. A compass rose and the Riverton oval stand at the top.
notes: Elm Avenue along the bottom is the Palmyra borough line, drawn with a dash-dot limit line; the 4th Street / Elm Avenue junction is the only Elm point used.
The junction of 2nd Street and Elm Avenue falls off the edge of the scan and was excluded; 4th Street and Thomas Avenue lies just off the top of the sheet.
50 ft. Thomas, Linden, Elm (Palmyra line) between 2nd and 4th; Morgan St. stub. Single part. 2nd/Elm off the image (excluded); only 4 junctions.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the southern blocks of Riverton between 4th Street on the left and Broad on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the cross streets run diagonally up the page to the right. Thomas Avenue forms the upper boundary, Linden Avenue crosses the middle, and Elm Avenue along the bottom is the borough line, drawn with a dash-dot limit line; the lettering 'See Map of Palmyra, N.J.' covers the ground beyond. A short stub of 5th Street enters Elm Avenue from the south near the lower left. The narrow lots of block 25, on the north side of Linden Avenue, and block 211, between Linden and Elm, hold rows of frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, many with outbuildings, with a few coloured pink for brick or tile. Between 4th Street and the first cross lots stand The Church of the Sacred Heart (R.C.) and its rectory, with lights, electricity, steam heat and furnace noted. At the right, near Broad, are a garage and repair shop for twelve cars, a gasoline storage tank, a tile-roofed building and a small row of dwellings numbered along Broad, where the railroad side of the street is drawn as a long strip. A compass rose and the Riverton oval stand at the top. Margins refer to Sheet 6 above, 8 at the left and 10 at the right. Four- and six-inch water pipes run in Thomas, Linden and Elm Avenues, with an eight-inch main in Broad.
notes: Broad is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap; its parcels are 28 to 35 ft wide against about 55 ft drawn, so street_widths was set to 55 for Broad Street on this sheet.
Elm Avenue along the bottom is the Palmyra borough line; 5th Street exists today only north of Main Street.

50 ft. Thomas, Linden, Elm (Palmyra line) between 4th and Broad; Church of the Sacred Heart (R.C.); 5th St. stub at bottom. Single part. street_widths Broad Street 55 ft (drawn) against 28-35 ft parcels; only 4 junctions.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the southern end of the Broad Street corridor and the blocks east of it, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The Pennsylvania Railroad (marked C. & A. Div.) runs diagonally up the left of the sheet, with a street named Broad on each side of the tracks, an 8-inch water main beside the eastern one, and a track branching off near the middle. A freight depot with its office and platforms stands beside the tracks near the top. East of the railroad the streets run square to the page: Thomas Avenue crosses the upper part, Linden Avenue the middle and Elm Avenue the bottom, and Harrison Avenue forms the right edge. Maple Lane is shown as a stub at the upper left. Blocks 216 and 224 hold rows of narrow lots with frame dwellings, outbuildings and a few pink-coloured tile or brick houses; block 225, below Elm Avenue, has larger detached houses on deeper lots. In the upper right corner, block 11 has dwellings and two small buildings coloured blue. A dash-dot line along the bottom marks the borough limits, and the lettering 'See Map of Palmyra, N.J.' covers the ground beyond. The large open area at the left, between the street and the sheet edge, is mostly blank and belongs to the neighbouring Sheet 6 and Sheet 9. A compass rose and the Riverton oval are drawn on the page, and the margin refers to Sheets 3, 6, 9, 11 and 7. Four-, six- and eight-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets.
notes: Broad east of the railroad is South Broad Street in OpenStreetMap, and the part of Elm Avenue east of Broad is Elm Terrace.
Harrison Avenue is today's Harrison Street.
Harrison Avenue / Thomas Avenue was excluded: Harrison is drawn with a jog at Thomas (see Sheet 11) and the point was 4 m off.

50 ft. P.R.R. diagonal with Broad on both sides; Thomas, Linden, Elm east to Harrison Av.; freight depot. Single part, drawn square to the page east of the tracks (rotation -29.5). Uses South Broad Street and Elm Terrace; Harrison/Thomas excluded (jog).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the southern blocks of Riverton between Harrison Avenue on the left and 7th Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the streets square to the page. Thomas Avenue crosses the upper part, Linden Avenue the middle and Elm Avenue the lower part, and the borough limits run along the bottom, beyond which the lettering 'See Map of Palmyra N.J.' covers the ground. A dash-dot match line (A to B) crosses the top, cutting through the northern blocks that continue on Sheet 3. Block 52, at the top, has rows of small dwellings with outbuildings and a blue-coloured structure on the match line. Blocks 217 and 218 hold regular rows of narrow lots, each with a frame dwelling of two or two and a half storeys and a small outbuilding, with a pink-coloured tile dwelling in block 217 and a long concrete base drawn in the lot fronting Linden Avenue. Block 226, below Elm Avenue, is largely open ground with a few dwellings, a pink tile dwelling and a pink outbuilding. A group of small dwellings stands along 7th Street between Linden and Elm Avenues. Harrison Avenue jogs to the west where it crosses Thomas Avenue. Four- and six-inch water pipes run in the streets, with fire hydrants at the corners. A compass rose and the Riverton oval are drawn on the sheet, and the margins refer to Sheets 3 above, 10 at the left and 12 at the right.
notes: Harrison Avenue is today's Harrison Street; Elm Avenue east of Broad is Elm Terrace in OpenStreetMap.
Harrison Street / Thomas Avenue was excluded because Harrison is drawn with a jog of about 225 px (28 ft) at Thomas Avenue and the junction is not a single point.
50 ft. Thomas, Linden, Elm between Harrison Av. and 7th; A-B match line with sheet 3 at top. Single part (rotation -27.6). Harrison/Thomas excluded (Harrison drawn with a 28 ft jog).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the east side of Riverton, from 7th Street to the borough limits and Cinnaminson Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page differently from the river-side sheets, with Main, Lippincott, Thomas, Linden and Elm running across it and 7th, Midway, 8th, Highway and Cherry Lane running up it. Cedar and Cinnaminson cross the top left corner, a short 9th Street runs north from Main, and Park runs south from Thomas to the Palmyra line. The western blocks between 7th and Highway are built up with detached frame dwellings; they include the First Church of Christ Scientist on Thomas Avenue near 7th Street and a pigeon house and concrete-block garage in block 12. East of Highway the land opens out: large lots and a few houses along Main and Cherry Lane, a stable and storage buildings, and the wide blocks 212, 252 and 228 north and east. South of Thomas Avenue and east of Park the sheet is taken up by a golf course with the Riverton Country Club house and bowling alleys on Park. The borough limits cross the lower right part diagonally, with Cinnaminson Township beyond, and run along the bottom edge, where a note refers to the map of Palmyra, N.J. A road is lettered along the bottom right edge. At the top right corner is the Public Service gas plant, marked not in operation with its buildings dismantled. Four- and six-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets.
notes: Elm Avenue is today's Elm Terrace in this stretch.
Cherry Lane is today's Shrewsbury Lane (north of the jog) and Shrewsbury Road; the modern Cherry Lane lies further east.
The modern 9th Street is not on the line of the 1925 9th Street; it was not used for control.
Riverton Country Club and golf course; First Church of Christ Scientist; Public Service gas plant, not in operation.

100 ft. East side: Cedar, Cinnaminson, Main, Lippincott, Thomas, Linden, Elm between 7th and the Cinnaminson Township line; 8th, Midway, Highway, Park, 9th, Cherry Lane; Riverton Country Club and golf course; Public Service gas plant. Single part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north end of Riverton on the Delaware River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The upper half is the nursery of Henry A. Dreer, Inc., seeds, plants and bulbs, between the river and Pompesse Creek, which runs along the top of the sheet: long ranges of glass-roofed greenhouses, a lily pond, potting, packing and shipping, bulb and bay tree houses, a summer house, boiler and engine rooms, storage sheds and wagon sheds, with a note on its 150 to 200 hands, watchman, heating, power and fire service. Below Fulton the residential streets of the old borough are laid out in a grid: Fulton, Cinnaminson, Howard, Main and Penn cross 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets, with Bank Avenue along the river bank at the left, a short stretch of Fifth Street at the right edge and Front Street entering at the bottom. The blocks hold large detached dwellings on deep lots. Named buildings are Christ Church with its rectory and the stone parish house at Howard and 4th Street, the Riverton Free Library on Main Street, a club house on Howard Street at 4th, an apartment house on Bank Avenue and The Lawn House, a boarding house, at Bank Avenue and Penn. A few dwellings stand on the river lots between Bank Avenue and the shore. Church Lane appears at the bottom right corner. The right edge beyond 4th Street is left blank and marked as Sheet 2, the bottom as Sheets 4, 5 and 6, and the top beyond the creek as Sheet 14. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: Henry A. Dreer, Inc. nursery (greenhouses) north of Fulton; the ground is now housing (Manor Court, Martha's Lane), and modern 3rd Street runs north of Fulton where no street is drawn in 1925 (junction excluded).
Christ Church, its rectory and parish house; Riverton Free Library; The Lawn House (boarding).
Bank Avenue is drawn with its river side open; its junctions were not detected and were not used for control.

100 ft. North end on the Delaware: Henry A. Dreer Inc. nursery works by Pompesse Creek; Bank Avenue, Fulton, Cinnaminson, Howard, Main, Penn between the river and 4th; Christ Church, free library. Single part.

sheet-14-1.description: The main part of Sheet 14 covers East Riverton, the grid of house lots in Cinnaminson Township north of Pompesse Creek, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broad Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy Division) run up the left third of the sheet, with Division Street to the west and Bannard Street along the east side of the tracks. Rowland and Land run parallel further east. Seven avenues cross them at regular intervals: Springfield, Snowden, Warrington, Belleview, Read, Randolph and Pompesse, from north to south. The blocks are large and mostly empty, numbered 1 to 24; scattered frame dwellings stand along Broad, Bannard, Randolph and the north side of Warrington, where a row of eight small dwellings fills block 16 at the east edge. At the top, north of Springfield Avenue, are the works of the Atlantic Paper Tube Co., Inc. (shipping, shop, stock and steel railroad car buildings), with a note that the Riverton Ice and Cold Storage plant lies 440 feet further on and is shown in the inset below. Other named buildings are the A.M.E. Baptist Church on Bannard Street at Belleview Avenue, a laundry on Randolph Avenue, a garage, a hotel and a transformer house west of Broad, and the Standard Oil Co. of N.J. oil and gasoline tanks at the bottom left by the creek. Pompesse Creek winds across the lower part of the sheet and runs along its bottom edge, the boundary with Riverton proper (Sheet 13). Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are drawn in most streets and an eight-inch pipe in Broad. The lower right corner holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Springfield Avenue is today's South Pleasant Avenue (Pleasant Avenue west of Broad Street).

The avenues are North ... west of Broad Street and South ... east of it today: Snowden, Warrington, Bellview (spelled Belleview in 1925), Read Street (Read Avenue in 1925), Randolph and Pompess (Pompesse in 1925) Avenues.
Division is today's Delaware Drive between Randolph and Pompess Avenues.
Broad Street junctions were not used for control: the 1925 Broad roadway and the railroad share one right of way.
Atlantic Paper Tube Co., Inc. works north of Springfield Avenue; Standard Oil Co. of N.J. tanks by Pompesse Creek.

100 ft. East Riverton (Cinnaminson Township) north of Pompesse Creek: Broad and the P.R.R., Division, Bannard, Rowland, Land; Springfield, Snowden, Warrington, Belleview, Read, Randolph, Pompesse Avenues; Atlantic Paper Tube Co. Two parts: main map and an inset at lower right (Broad and Bannard further north, Riverton Ice & Cold Storage Co.) with its own north arrow.

sheet-14-2.description: This inset in the lower right corner of Sheet 14, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and framed by a heavy line, continues East Riverton north along Broad Street beyond the main map. A printed note at its foot says that it lies 440 feet beyond the Atlantic Paper Tube Co. works shown above (at the top of the main part), and the main part carries the matching note. The inset shows Broad Street with an eight-inch water pipe, the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy Division) tracks east of it, and Bannard Street curving in towards the tracks at the north end. West of Broad, in block 21, stands a row of nine small frame dwellings. East of Bannard, in block 24, are the buildings of the Riverton Ice & Cold Storage Co.: a sorting room, two cold storage buildings (one of tile walls, concrete slab roof and steel girders, built 1919), an ice machine room, a tank room, an office and a warehouse, with a description of its power, heating, lighting and fire protection (two Worthington fire pumps, two hydrants with hose, a Buffalo steam pump) and of its water supply from a dug well. A few outbuildings stand further east. No cross street is drawn, so the inset was placed from the main part of the sheet using the printed 440-foot distance and the line of Broad Street, at the same scale and orientation.
